articles.title: Câmara dos EUA barra pedido de impeachment de secretário de Guerra | G1
articles.standfirst: Em manobra republicana, Câmara devolveu impeachment de Hegseth a comissão e adiou votação no plenário. Democratas queriam análise direta pelos deputados.
articles.summary: Em manobra republicana, Câmara devolveu impeachment de Hegseth a comissão e adiou votação no plenário. Democratas queriam análise direta pelos deputados.
articles.body:
Secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth, durante coletiva à imprensa no Pentágono — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

A Câmara dos Deputados dos Estados Unidos aprovou nesta terça-feira (10) uma manobra republicana para barrar a votação do pedido de impeachment contra Pete Hegseth, secretário de Guerra do governo Trump e chefe do Pentágono.

A proposta foi aprovada por 211 votos a 204. Com a decisão, os artigos de impeachment apresentados pelo deputado republicano Thomas Massie serão enviados à Comissão de Assuntos Judiciários da Câmara, controlada pelos republicanos.

Na prática, a decisão impede que as acusações sejam submetidas à votação do plenário neste momento.

Como os republicanos têm maioria na comissão, o partido passa a controlar a análise do pedido e pode impedir que ele avance para uma votação pelos demais deputados.

A proposta também pode ficar parada no colegiado até o fim da atual legislatura, em janeiro de 2027.

O pedido foi apresentado na segunda-feira (9) por Massie, que pertence ao mesmo partido de Donald Trump. A iniciativa prevê oito artigos de impeachment contra Hegseth.

Mais cedo nesta terça, Hegseth se defendeu das acusações em entrevista a jornalistas no Pentágono. O secretário chamou o pedido de impeachment contra ele de "farsa" e um "espetáculo político" que fracassará. Hegseth também atacou o autor da proposta, Thomas Massie.

"É um espetáculo político, um manifesto pessoal movido por ego e ressentimento, planejado para os últimos dias de um homem no Congresso, com o objetivo de prejudicar este presidente, este país e, o que é mais irresponsável, os guerreiros que o defendem. É uma farsa e uma manobra política, e todos sabem disso", afirmou.

Logo após o resultado, o Departamento de Guerra publicou em uma rede social uma imagem gerada por inteligência artificial que mostra Massie chorando.

"A tentativa do ex-deputado, insatisfeito e afastado do cargo, de aprovar o impeachment do secretário Hegseth FRACASSOU!", escreveu o departamento.

O presidente Donald Trump também comemorou o resultado. Em uma publicação nas redes sociais, ele afirmou que a tentativa dos democratas de aprovar o impeachment de Hegseth "fracassou miseravelmente".

Trump disse que todos os republicanos, com exceção de Thomas Massie, votaram a favor do secretário e atribuiu o resultado às vitórias militares dos Estados Unidos na Venezuela e no Irã, além dos números recordes de recrutamento nas Forças Armadas.

O pedido de impeachment ocorre após a derrota do Partido Republicano nas urnas nas eleições de meio de mandato, as midterms.

A sigla do presidente Trump perdeu o controle tanto na Câmara quanto no Senado, no que a imprensa americana chamou de "onda azul" — em referência à cor do Partido Democrata.

A guerra no Irã é apontada como um dos principais fatores que provocaram a derrocada republicana e colocou Hegseth, chefe do Pentágono na mira tanto de democratas quanto de seus correligionários republicanos.

Para Sandra Cohen, colunista do g1 , o secretário de Guerra estava na berlinda antes mesmo do desastre eleitoral republicano da semana passada, mas rapidamente ele passou a ser o bode expiatório da eleição .

As acusações de Thomas Massie contra Hegseth

O deputado americano Thomas Massie (republicano do Kentucky) concede entrevista coletiva sobre sua proposta de impeachment do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth, no Capitólio, em Washington, nos Estados Unidos, em 9 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein

O deputado Thomas Massie reuniu oito acusações contra Pete Hegseth. O relatório foi lido no plenário da Câmara na segunda.

Para o republicano, o secretário de Guerra abusou dos poderes do cargo e desrespeitou a Constituição americana ao executar e manter operações militares sem a autorização exigida por lei.

Confira abaixo as 8 acusações do processo de impeachment contra Hegseth:

Travar a guerra contra o Irã sem autorização do Congresso .

Desobedecer à ordem de retirada do Irã , mesmo após Câmara e Senado aprovarem uma resolução para retirar as tropas.

Manter operações no Irã além do prazo legal de 60 dias previsto em lei.

Enfraquecer a proteção de civis ao reduzir mecanismos de prevenção e investigação de mortes causadas pelas operações militares.

Autorizar execuções extrajudiciais de suspeitos de tráfico , por meio de ataques contra embarcações suspeitas de transportar drogas no Mar do Caribe e no Oceano Pacífico.

Intimidar o senador democrata Mark Kelly , após o parlamentar defender que militares podem se recusar a cumprir ordens ilegais.

Capturar Nicolás Maduro sem autorização do Congresso .

Conduzir a guerra no Iêmen sem autorização do Congresso .

Como funciona o processo de impeachment?

A Constituição dos EUA determina que cabe à Câmara dos Deputados iniciar processos de impeachment. Já o Senado é responsável por julgar as acusações e decidir se investigado deve ser condenado e afastado do cargo.

O processo pode começar com uma investigação feita por deputados.

Depois de analisar as acusações, a Câmara vota se o secretário deve sofrer impeachment.

Para que o impeachment seja aprovado na Câmara, é necessária maioria simples dos votos , ou seja, mais da metade dos parlamentares presentes.

No caso de Hegseth, o deputado Thomas Massie apresentou diretamente um pedido de impeachment, sem passar por uma investigação de uma comissão da Câmara.

Se a Câmara tivesse aprovado o impeachment, o processo seguiria para o Senado, onde os parlamentares decidiriam se Hegseth deveria ser condenado e afastado do cargo.

Pete Hegseth e Donald Trump em foto de arquivo. — Foto: Reuters/Kevin Lamarque

Apesar da pressão política, o afastamento de Hegseth já era considerado improvável.

Fontes do Congresso ouvidas pela agência Reuters avaliavam que o impeachment até poderia conseguir votos suficientes para avançar na Câmara, mesmo com os republicanos ainda no controle da Casa. Os democratas só assumirão a maioria em 3 de janeiro.

No entanto, a situação seria diferente no Senado. Para condenar Hegseth seriam necessários votos de dois terços dos parlamentares. Atualmente, os republicanos ocupam 53 das 100 cadeiras, o que tornaria esse resultado pouco provável.

O único secretário de Guerra dos EUA que já sofreu impeachment foi William Belknap, em 1876. Ele renunciou ao cargo antes da votação na Câmara, mas o processo continuou no Senado, que acabou o absolvendo por falta de votos.

articles.title: Guerra da Ucrânia: europeus defendem cessar-fogo como pré-requisito para negociações de paz concretas; Rússia descarta | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela primeira vez em 9 meses, representantes da Rússia e da Ucrânia sentaram à mesa para negociar o fim da guerra. O encontro em Abu Dhabi teve a mediação dos Estados Unidos.
articles.summary: Pela primeira vez em 9 meses, representantes da Rússia e da Ucrânia sentaram à mesa para negociar o fim da guerra. O encontro em Abu Dhabi teve a mediação dos Estados Unidos.
articles.body:
Pela primeira vez em nove meses, representantes da Rússia e da Ucrânia sentaram à mesa para negociar o fim da guerra. O encontro em Abu Dhabi teve a mediação dos Estados Unidos .

Primeiro, os representantes da Ucrânia se reuniram com os enviados dos Estados Unidos, de países europeus e da Otan , a aliança militar do Ocidente. Só depois com os enviados da Rússia. Moscou não aceitou a participação direta dos europeus na mesa principal. Os Estados Unidos agora querem mudar isso.

“Vai ser essencial para avançarmos”, afirmou o enviado americano Jared Kushner, genro do presidente Donald Trump.

Depois de quase quatro horas, a trilateral terminou sem qualquer anúncio. Lá se vão nove meses. A rodada anterior foi realizada em Genebra, em fevereiro de 2026. Só que a guerra com o Irã desviou a atenção do conflito mais sangrento na Europa desde a Segunda Guerra Mundial. Para piorar, a aproximação de Washington e Moscou aumentou a desconfiança de Kiev e de aliados do Velho Continente.

Guerra da Ucrânia: europeus defendem cessar-fogo como pré-requisito para negociações de paz concretas; Rússia descarta — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Em visita à Dinamarca, o presidente da Ucrânia, Volodymyr Zelensky , classificou a reunião desta terça-feira (10) como “ construtiva e bastante substancial ”. Na França, o secretário de Estado americano, Marco Rubio, também descreveu as conversas como “ muito produtivas ”. Rubio reconheceu que os europeus " fazem parte da solução a longo prazo ”.

Os europeus defendem um cessar-fogo incondicional como pré-requisito para negociações de paz concretas. Mas a Rússia descarta. O chanceler Sergei Lavrov disse que uma trégua ajudaria a Ucrânia a se reorganizar militarmente.

A Rússia ocupa cerca de um quinto do país vizinho. O controle do leste ucraniano continua um dos principais obstáculos. Nos bastidores, fala-se de alguma flexibilidade dos dois lados. As negociações continuam nesta quarta-feira (11), com certo otimismo nas declarações, mas grandes distâncias ainda à mesa.

articles.title: Mega-Sena 3084 teve vencedor em Santa Catarina? | G1
articles.summary: Apostador de Joinville acertou cinco números.
articles.body:
Uma aposta simples feita digitalmente em Joinville , no Norte de Santa Catarina , acertou cinco dos seis números sorteados do concurso 3084 da Mega-Sena na noite desta terça-feira (10). O apostador levou R$ 28.344,40 .

Veja os números sorteados: 06 - 14 - 22 - 30 - 31 - 37

Outras 106 apostas de Santa Catarina acertaram quatro números e levaram R$ 518,64 cada.

O próximo sorteio da Mega-Sena está previsto para quinta (12). A estimativa é de R$ 20 milhões para quem acertar os seis números.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e o tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Brasileiro relata apreensão com tempestade que pode provocar ventos de até 140 km/h em Portugal: 'Canais mandaram estocar comida' | G1
articles.standfirst: Paraibano Samuel Gualberto é natural de Malta, na Paraíba, e mora em Lisboa, um dos locais que podem ser atingidos por tempestade em Portugal, considerada de grandes proporções.
articles.summary: Paraibano Samuel Gualberto é natural de Malta, na Paraíba, e mora em Lisboa, um dos locais que podem ser atingidos por tempestade em Portugal, considerada de grandes proporções.
articles.body:
Um paraibano que mora em Lisboa , em Portugal, relatou ao g1 a apreensão com a chegada de uma tempestade que pode provocar ventos de até 140 km/h nos próximos dias, segundo o Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA). O governo português emitiu um alerta para o fenômeno, com medidas preventivas que começam a valer nesta quarta-feira (11), incluindo o fechamento de escolas e de serviços públicos não essenciais.

O paraibano Samuel Gualberto, natural de Malta , no interior da Paraíba, está em Portugal para cursar um mestrado em psicologia na Universidade de Lisboa. Ele mora na capital portuguesa com outros dois paraibanos, naturais de João Pessoa , e uma pessoa de Fortaleza , no Ceará.

"Outros canais têm recomendado estocar um pouco de comida e vários serviços que não são essenciais também já alertaram que vão paralisar durante a quarta.Por exemplo, a academia mandou email pra gente dizendo que não estaria aberta durante a quarta", ressaltou.

Segundo Samuel, além das medidas anunciadas pelo governo, moradores também receberam orientações para se preparar para a tempestade, incluindo a recomendação de manter alimentos em casa . A universidade onde estuda, por exemplo, informou que não funcionará durante a quarta-feira.

Conhecida como tempestade Charles, a passagem do fenômeno também levou à suspensão de atividades ao ar livre e ao fechamento de parques, florestas e jardins a partir desta quarta-feira (11) .

Governo português mandou aviso sobre tempestade em Portugal para habitantes — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Samuel Gualberto

Samuel também recebeu alertas da Defesa Civil portuguesa diretamente no celular sobre as condições climáticas previstas para o país . Entre as recomendações das autoridades está a orientação para que os moradores evitem sair de casa durante a passagem da tempestade. Veja a imagem abaixo.

Sobre a expectativa para a chegada do fenômeno, o paraibano descreveu um sentimento de “incerteza”. Ele explicou que ainda está há pouco tempo em Portugal e que, por isso, não sabe exatamente o que esperar. Segundo Samuel, conhecidos portugueses também demonstram preocupação, apesar de já terem vivenciado outros episódios de condições climáticas extremas.

"Então, a gente também tá há pouco tempo aqui. Mas, é uma sensação de incerteza. A gente não sabe o que pode esperar. Pelo relatos que a gente tem de outras pessoas, pode realmente acontecer de ter ventos muito fortes que derrubam árvores, que arrancam placas nas ruas, mas não chegaram a relatar ter experienciado falta de energia por muitas horas, um tempo muito prolongado. A gente percebe que tem alguns colegas portugueses que, sim, estão bem preocupados com isso", relatou.

Apesar da apreensão, Samuel acredita que a localização de onde mora pode amenizar os possíveis impactos. Ele explicou que está em um bairro situado em uma área mais alta de Lisboa e, por isso, não espera enfrentar transtornos tão significativos.

Tempestade em Portugal com ventos de 140 km/h

Imagem ilustrativa de outro ciclone/iclone Hinnamnor — Foto: Cooperative Institute for Meteorological Satellite Studies

A Tempestade Charles é um intenso ciclone extratropical que se formou no Oceano Atlântico e avança rapidamente em direção ao continente europeu, provocando uma queda acentuada da pressão atmosférica.

O Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA) prevê um cenário de chuva intensa e ventos fortes, sobretudo nas regiões Centro e Sul de Portugal. As rajadas de vento poderão atingir os 140 km/h, com possibilidade de velocidades ainda superiores.

Segundo as previsões, o centro da área de baixa pressão deverá entrar no território continental pela região da Grande Lisboa, embora ainda haja incertezas quanto à sua trajetória.

Oito distritos estão sob aviso vermelho, o nível máximo de alerta meteorológico: Leiria, Santarém, Lisboa, Setúbal, Portalegre, Évora, Beja e Faro.

Já a Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente (APA) alertou para o risco de inundações em 101 municípios, devido ao elevado volume de chuva previsto.

articles.title: 2026 Midterms: Blue wave or anti-establishment backlash?
articles.summary: Emma Vigeland and Olivia Troye join Josh Rushing to discuss the fallout of the 2026 midterm elections.
articles.body:
The midterms are over, and Democrats have scored a decisive victory, exceeding even their most optimistic expectations. But does this result signal a country turning blue – or a country simply fed up with the status quo? And how much of this was a rejection of a system, rather than an endorsement of the Democratic Party?

Josh Rushing is joined by Emma Vigeland, cohost of The Majority Report, and Olivia Troye, who served as a national security adviser to former Vice President Mike Pence, to unpack the results and what they reveal about the state of American politics.

Contributors: Emma Vigeland – Cohost, The Majority Report Olivia Troye – Former national security adviser to Mike Pence

articles.title: Representantes dos empresários, trabalhadores, Congresso e Governo participam de audiência pública sobre escala 5x2 | G1
articles.standfirst: O ministro do Supremo Flávio Dino presidiu uma audiência pública. Ele é relator de duas ações que propõem adiar o cronograma de implementação da nova jornada de trabalho.
articles.summary: O ministro do Supremo Flávio Dino presidiu uma audiência pública. Ele é relator de duas ações que propõem adiar o cronograma de implementação da nova jornada de trabalho.
articles.body:
O ministro do Supremo Flávio Dino presidiu uma audiência pública para discutir os questionamentos sobre a entrada em vigor da escala 5x2.

O ministro Flávio Dino é relator de duas ações que propõem adiar o cronograma de implementação da nova jornada de trabalho. A escala 5x2, aprovada em outubro pelo Congresso, reduz o limite semanal de 44 horas para 42 horas, a partir de 16 de dezembro. E, um ano depois, a jornada máxima passará a ser de 40 horas.

O debate nesta terça-feira (10) reuniu representantes dos empresários, de trabalhadores, do Congresso e o ministro do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho. A advogada Luciana Diniz, da Confederação Nacional do Comércio, explicou a dificuldade das empresas para se adaptarem em um prazo tão curto:

"A emenda, ela concede 60 dias para reorganizar as jornadas de dezenas de milhões de brasileiros e de dezenas de empresas, e assim como negociar milhares de negociações coletivas. Para comparação, a reforma trabalhista teve um prazo de 120 dias de transição. Os 60 dias são sufocantes para tantas atividades que precisam ser feitas tanto pelos sindicatos e pelas empresas. Lá fora, a gente pode trazer como referência que o Chile deu cinco anos para chegar a 40 horas. Colômbia também cinco anos. O México, que reformou a Constituição esse ano, ele traz um prazo de cerca de dez meses só para a primeira equalização".

A Confederação Nacional da Indústria estima que a nova jornada pode aumentar os custos de mão de obra em até 33% com o pagamento de horas extras ou contratação de novos empregados. O diretor jurídico da entidade também defendeu adiar o início da escala 5x2.

"Nós temos, efetivamente, que nesta fase discutir o que fazer sobre o dia 16 de dezembro. Mas precisamos fazer isso de uma tal forma que a transição seja suave, bemfazeja e que, ao mesmo tempo, garanta que a atividade econômica não vai ter problemas de suprimento de demanda de mão de obra", diz Alexandre Vitorino, diretor jurídico da CNI.

A Nova Central Sindical de Trabalhadores se manifestou contra a ampliação do prazo.

"A redução da jornada e ampliação do repouso não estão em negociação. E concordamos, queremos discutir os caminhos da implementação, respeitando as particularidades das categorias específicas, preservando os empregos e assegurando direitos conquistados", diz Sônia Zerino, presidente da Nova Central Sindical de Trabalhadores.

Representantes dos empresários, trabalhadores, Congresso e Governo participam de audiência pública sobre escala 5x2 — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O ministro do Trabalho, Luiz Marinho, disse que vai se reunir com o presidente Lula quando ele voltar da Ásia, na segunda-feira (16), para definir os termos do decreto sobre a redução da jornada. Ele disse que foi procurado por diversas entidades empresariais que se anteciparam às mudanças:

"As empresas que toparam, que procuraram, chegaram a acordo, encontraram solução, encontraram caminhos. Resta a gente ter coragem de pensar uma oportunidade que o Brasil há muito tempo não aciona, com raríssimas exceções, que é fazer os acordos nacionais de setor de economia".

A decisão do ministro Flávio Dino não vai mexer na lei que acabou com a escala 6x1. O ministro disse que vai decidir até a sexta-feira (13) sobre as ações que questionam a transição para a escala 5x2. Ele adiantou que não haverá mudança direta da jornada para 40 horas por semana sem passar pela transição prevista em lei, de 42 horas semanais. Dino também deve permitir que negociações coletivas possam flexibilizar a compensação dos dias de folga, sem limitador mensal ou semanal. As decisões, segundo o ministro, serão submetidas ao plenário do STF . Ainda não há data para esse julgamento.

articles.title: Mãe banca tratamento da filha mesmo após Justiça obrigar plano | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso é parte dos problemas enfrentados por clientes da GoCare na região de Campinas. Há um ano, empresa também foi alvo de reclamações de usuários.
articles.summary: Caso é parte dos problemas enfrentados por clientes da GoCare na região de Campinas. Há um ano, empresa também foi alvo de reclamações de usuários.
articles.body:
A dona de casa Amanda Lopes assumiu os custos particulares do tratamento da filha Valentina desde o início de novembro, mesmo após a Justiça obrigar o plano de saúde GoCare a fornecer os aparelhos de assistência domiciliar.

O caso é parte dos problemas enfrentados por clientes da operadora na região de Campinas (SP). Segundo reclamações recebidas pela EPTV , emissora afiliada da TV Globo , a empresa tem deixado de oferecer consultas e tratamentos por conta de um suposto problema financeiro .

"Liminares que estão ganhas, determinadas por juiz, e até o momento não estão cumprindo nada. Eles simplesmente estão deixando a Valentina ao léu, deixando ela sem assistência, sem nada. É o que eles querem que aconteça, parece que o pior com a minha filha", comentou Amanda.

"O meu sentimento no momento, além da tristeza, é de impotência em alguns momentos. Mas eu tenho esperança, né? Porque a gente está tentando fazer de tudo para as coisas da Valentina acontecerem, porque ela é uma criança e ela precisa desses cuidados", desabafou.

Amanda Lopes tem bancado tratamento da filha Valentina — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Há quase um ano, a EPTV mostrou denúncias de usuários contra a GoCare. Na época, os relatos foram de consultas, quimioterapias e cirurgias que deixaram de ser realizadas .

Em nota, o advogado Bruno Conceição, que representa o plano de saúde, lamentou os transtornos relatados e disse que a operadora vem "empreendendo todos os esforços para a regularização de todos os atendimentos" e o "restabelecimento, na maior brevidade possível, das coberturas e assistências devidas aos beneficiários".

A GoCare também afirmou que vem sendo acompanhada pela Agência Nacional de Saúde (ANS) em razão de anormalidade econômico-financeira . "Todas essas questões são de pleno conhecimento da ANS, autarquia reguladora do setor, com a qual a GoCare mantém atuação transparente e colaborativa", pontuou.

A ANS foi procurada, mas não respondeu até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Ana Carolina Pinton Figueiredo teve tumor encontrado no cérebro — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

O descumprimento de terapias também atinge pacientes oncológicos. Após vencer um nódulo na mama, a terapeuta ocupacional Ana Carolina Pinton Figueiredo foi diagnosticada com a doença no cérebro.

Ela retomou a quimioterapia e conseguiu controlar o avanço em maio de 2026, mas a GoCare suspendeu as sessões e a paciente já está há dois meses sem a medicação .

"Disseram que o plano está falindo, que não vão me fornecer, que tem muita inadimplência, que eles não têm dinheiro", relatou.

Um exame realizado em outubro mostrou que o tumor voltou a crescer, obrigando a paciente a entrar na fila do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

"Eu espero um tratamento no Mário Gatti e que o convênio arrume um outro convênio para mim, porque são eles que têm que arrumar", disparou.

Casos de falha na prestação de serviços médicos têm levado pacientes à Justiça. O escritório da advogada especialista em direito à saúde Thais Pedi Silva registrou um aumento no número de casos nos últimos meses.

"Todo mundo que contrata um plano de saúde precisa ter a garantia de que vai poder utilizar esse plano de saúde quando precisar, como é o caso. E o Poder Judiciário resguarda esse direito", comentou.

A principal orientação para situações de urgência em que a operadora descumpre as liminares é solicitar o bloqueio financeiro da empresa .

"Para que seja pago o tratamento com os valores bloqueados da conta da operadora", explicou Thais.

articles.title: 'No flights will shift from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai airport': Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed Mumbai airport operator’s plan to shift international flights to 14 destinations to Navi Mumbai
articles.body: MUMBAI: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has opposed Mumbai airport operator’s plan to shift international flights to 14 destinations to Navi Mumbai airport from next summer, saying no flights would be moved out of Mumbai.He has written to the union civil aviation minister on the issue.Fadnavis on Tuesday said he has proposed an alternative sequence for Terminal 1 (T1) redevelopment that would allow the existing terminal to remain operational until its replacement is ready.“I have written to them to first develop Terminal 1B, shift 1A to 1B and then take down the existing 1A terminal,” Fadnavis said.His proposal would allow the airport to demolish and reconstruct T1 in stages rather than shut it down entirely before starting construction of the replacement.The Airports Authority of India (AAI), a central government entity, holds 26% stake in Mumbai airport, with the remaining 74% held by Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL).The issue of moving some flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai airport has been contentious.Last month, Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) informed airlines about its plans to reduce international operations at Terminal 2 (T2) by a third from the Summer 2027 schedule, beginning March-end, to accommodate 5 million passengers per annum (mppa) of domestic traffic displaced by the first phase of T1 demolition.Last week, AAHL informed the ministry that it plans to move flights connecting Mumbai with 14 international destinations to Navi Mumbai from next summer.The destinations are Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah.MIAL has told airlines that it cannot accommodate their requested Summer 2027 slots and that a temporary transition out of T2 will be necessary.The proposed shift has faced resistance from airlines. The International Air Transport Association (IATA), which represents airlines globally, had urged the ministry to adopt a phased redevelopment approach, whereby portions of T1 would be demolished and reconstructed sequentially to avoid a wholesale loss of capacity.The entire 15-mppa (million passengers per annum) T1 is scheduled to be demolished by March 2028, with reconstruction beginning only thereafter.The new T1 is expected to be ready by December 2030. Airlines sources said that shutting T1 completely would leave Mumbai airport with a substantial capacity deficit for three years or more."The operational complexity at T1 stems from its fragmented infrastructure, with T1A, T1B and T1C not functioning as independent, full-scale terminals," said a source."While T1A remains unusable due to infrastructure constraints and obsolete equipment, T1C has only six contact gates and depends on T1B for passenger check-in. Passenger processing is consequently split across T1B's two security hold areas and T1C, restricting passenger movement and affecting asset utilisation and service quality," the source added.The operational interdependence between T1 and T2 also extends to the airside. MIAL has proposed a 3.042-km underground airside tunnel connecting the T1 and T2 aprons, as well as additional aircraft parking stands proposed south of runway 09-27.Currently, when T2 runs short of parking stands, some aircraft are parked at the T1 apron, requiring passengers and baggage to be transported between the two via a perimeter road and runway 14-32.The airport operator cited lengthy transfer times and monsoon-related delays as reasons for the proposed tunnel.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Frank Sinatra's former wife Nancy Barbato lived in this Beverly Hills estate for years; the one-acre property is now available for $27,495 a month
articles.summary: Nancy Barbato, the first wife of legendary singer Frank Sinatra, spent years living in a Beverly Hills estate that became closely associated with the
articles.body: Nancy Barbato, the first wife of legendary singer Frank Sinatra, spent years living in a Beverly Hills estate that became closely associated with the Sinatra family. The property, set on more than an acre of landscaped land, has now attracted attention again after entering the luxury rental market. Located on North Beverly Drive, the residence combines its historical connection to the family with renovated interiors, extensive entertainment areas and private outdoor spaces. According to Realtor, the home was offered for $27,495 a month, giving prospective tenants an opportunity to live in a property with a distinctive Hollywood connection.Nancy Barbato’s Beverly Hills estate returns to the rental marketThe property at 1121 North Beverly Drive in Beverly Hills is known as the Sinatra Residence, reflecting its connection to Nancy Barbato and her former husband. Realtor reported that the house had entered the rental market for the first time in more than 35 years, making it an unusual opportunity for those interested in celebrity-associated real estate.Barbato lived in the residence for years, using it as a home for family and friends. She and Frank Sinatra married in 1939 and had three children together: Nancy Sinatra Jr., Frank Sinatra Jr. and Tina Sinatra. Although the couple divorced in 1951, their relationship remained close, and Barbato continued to be an important figure in the singer's life.The estate's appeal goes beyond its celebrity history. Its secluded setting, generous grounds and traditional ranch-style design give it a character distinct from many contemporary luxury properties in the area.What does the property offer beyond its Hollywood historyThe estate has been renovated while retaining much of its original exterior appearance. Realtor reported that the property remained recognisable from the time Barbato lived there, even as the interiors were updated to suit contemporary luxury living.The house covers approximately 4,800 square feet and includes 5 bedrooms, 7 bathrooms and several spaces for relaxation and entertaining. One of the bedrooms is designated as a maid's room, reflecting the property's sizable layout.According to the listing on Compass website, the residence is furnished, allowing tenants to move in without having to arrange furniture separately. Hardwood floors, stone tiles in the kitchen and bathrooms, and carpeting in the bedrooms create different finishes across the interiors.The living room is one of the house's features. The vaulted ceiling, skylights and French doors allow for lots of natural light and the doors open to the back yard. A grand piano and a veranda further contribute to the room's character.The interiors are designed for entertaining guestsThe house has a number of spaces designed for entertaining guests, not just for everyday living. Realtor highlighted a formal dining room with a wet bar that seats three and a dedicated wine room.These features lend themselves to dinner parties and larger gatherings in the residence. The entertainment areas are complemented by comfortable living spaces, with the furnishing arrangement intended to make the property feel both luxurious and welcoming.The veranda offers another space to enjoy the outdoors while the living room creates a central gathering space inside. Together, these spaces connect the property's traditional residential character with its modern presentation.The one-acre grounds provide privacy and outdoor amenitiesAnother huge part of the draw is the estate’s outdoor setting. The property sits behind private gates on more than an acre of landscaped land across from Coldwater Canyon Park. The grounds feel private and secluded considering that the house is in Beverly Hills.The backyard wraps around the residence and includes a recently installed raised infinity pool. A large patio provides space for outdoor gatherings, with a built-in barbecue and preparation station adding to its entertaining facilities.The listing also notes a three-car garage plus extra parking on the driveway. The property’s outdoor appeal is enhanced by views of the surrounding treetops and city, and the gated entrance separates the residence from its surroundings.What happened to the estate after Nancy Barbato's deathBarbato remained the property's owner until her death in 2018. The residence subsequently changed hands in 2020 for $6.25 million.Realtor reported that another Beverly Hills property owned by Barbato's daughter sold for $3 million in 2023. That residence retained several original mid-century modern details, including mirrored walls, parquet flooring and a distinctive martini bar.The North Beverly Drive estate, meanwhile, offers a different connection to the family through its long association with Barbato and her years living there.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Mojtaba Khamenei aide's chilling '40 years' warning surfaces amid US push for Iran deal
articles.summary: Mohsen Rezaei once warned that ceasefire talks could last decades, as JD Vance reportedly reached out to him about resuming U.S.-Iran peace talks.
articles.body: Iran's top security official, who reportedly received a letter from Vice President JD Vance about resuming peace talks, warned in a resurfaced interview that wartime negotiations with Tehran could drag on for decades, and during which both sides should "be prepared to fight." Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), now serves as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and acts as a key aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. He also helped shape Tehran's military strategy during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War. That eight-year conflict ended after Iran's then-supreme leader, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, accepted a U.N.-brokered cease-fire that he famously likened to drinking from a "poisoned chalice." JD VANCE RETURNS TO WASHINGTON AFTER 16 HOURS OF IRAN PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE IN PAKISTAN "Ceasefire means an unfinished war," Rezaei had said of the war in a 2006 interview with the Iranian publication Baztab. An English translation of the interview is preserved by George Washington University's National Security Archive. Asked whether both sides would remain in their positions and begin talks, Rezaei replied: "Yes. Negotiations can take 30 to 40 years and during that time Iran and Iraq should be prepared to fight." Two decades after suggesting negotiations could drag on for years, Washington has reportedly been seeking talks with Rezaei, a key power player in Iran’s current military leadership. Vance sent him a letter proposing renewed peace talks between the United States and Iran in October, the Wall Street Journal reported. Iran said it had received a letter from Vance but had not responded, according to Iranian state media. The semi-official Tasnim News Agency said Iran was awaiting U.S. compliance with its conditions, warning that "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable." TRUMP SAYS IRAN DEAL ‘LARGELY NEGOTIATED’ AS 84-DAY WAR NEARS POSSIBLE END In June, President Donald Trump had posted a warning on Truth Social that Iran had taken too long to come to terms and would "pay the price," while on Monday, he also said that Iran wanted a deal but warned that another U.S. strike could be about five times as large as the previous. "We could knock it out fast, or we could knock it out over a short, not a long period of time," Trump said during a C-SPAN interview on "Washington Journal Primetime." "I can tell you that Iran would like to make a deal, and we'll find out whether that'll happen," Trump said of the current timeframe. Rezaei however, has continued to maintain a defiant stance toward Washington, writing on X on Nov. 9: "The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government," he wrote before adding that "Washington flails like a desperate gambler." "FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks. "Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER. Time to SURRENDER to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out," he said. Following the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, Rezaei also claimed Iran had defeated Washington militarily and politically. He warned of a "devastating response" to another attack and declared it was time for Washington to "SURRENDER." RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY' Rezaei also rejected reports of ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations or any planned meeting in Qatar, accusing Washington of spreading false claims to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices. He reiterated that Tehran would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions were met. Rezaei has spent more than four decades in Iran's defense establishment. He commanded the IRGC from 1981 to 1997, overseeing operations during the Iran-Iraq War. In the 2006 Baztab interview, Rezaei also detailed how Iranian leaders distinguished their public rhetoric from military strategy. Although Khomeini and other Iranian officials called for "fighting till Saddam is toppled" and "until the nuisance is eradicated," Rezaei said Tehran's actual strategy was "fighting up to a victory." At the time, Iran's battlefield gains, he suggested, were meant to strengthen Tehran's negotiating position rather than achieve total conquest. IRAN VOWS ‘ASTONISHING’ STRIKES AND LIFTS MISSILE-RANGE LIMIT AS US TARGETS LAND ROUTES "The world did not pay attention to the slogans," Rezaei said in the interview, adding that foreign governments and intelligence agencies focused on Iranian leaders' actions and diplomatic positions. Rezaei also said Iran had struggled to turn battlefield gains into diplomatic victories because it lacked international alliances and influence at the United Nations. Rezaei has since faced U.S. sanctions and international scrutiny. The Trump administration first sanctioned him Jan. 10, 2020, under an executive order targeting senior Iranian officials appointed by the supreme leader. Rezaei had also been accused of involvement in the July 1994 bombing of the Argentine Israelite Mutual Association Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, which killed 85 people. articles.title: Woman apologizes for making racist gestures outside Ole Miss students’ apartment
articles.summary: The University of Mississippi is investigating the incident after a video caught two women mimicking apes outside three Black students’ front door.
articles.body: One of the two young women seen on a viral video making racist gestures outside the apartment of three Black Ole Miss students apologized for her actions. Alaina Kunes, 18, said in a statement Tuesday that she did not know the people who lived in the apartment and was “unaware of their race” until the Ring doorbell camera video that captured the moment Friday gained national attention. The video shows Kunes and two other women walking by the front door of the off-campus apartment where the three Black Ole Miss students live. Kunes is seen beating her chest. She and a second woman, who has not been identified and has not commented on the incident, make ape noises. A third woman in the video just walks by without stopping at the door. “To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize,” Kunes said in her statement. “I recognize my actions were insensitive, inappropriate, and deeply harmful.” Kunes said she apologized to the women who live in the apartment directly. “I pray they will forgive me,” she said. “I can never truly understand the pain I have caused them and it was never my intention. These girls deserve to feel seen and understood and what I did is not a reflection of who I am trying to become,” Kunes said. The University of Mississippi launched an investigation into the incident, Shawnboda Mead, the school’s vice chancellor for student affairs, said in an email sent to the campus Sunday. In it, Mead described the viral video as “showing University of Mississippi students engaging in racist gestures directed toward other students.” Kunes has since withdrawn from the university, a source close to the 18-year-old told NBC News. It’s unclear what the enrollment status is of the other women in the video. The University of Mississippi did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday. Tasha Bolton, the mother of one of the three Black Ole Miss students, wrote about the incident in a Facebook post Saturday. Bolton said her daughter is a freshman at the university and lives in the off-campus apartment with two Black roommates. She described the women filmed on the doorbell camera as her daughter’s upstairs neighbors. “This is absolutely disgusting and unacceptable. College is supposed to be a place where young adults can learn, grow, and feel safe,” Bolton said about the video in her post. “We want answers. Specifically, what steps will be taken to address this behavior and ensure accountability?” Kunes said she intends to fully cooperate with the university’s investigation. “I would have never intentionally made those noises or gestures toward a person of color,” she said in her statement apologizing for the incident. “I understand the seriousness of this situation and remain committed to taking responsibility and learning from this embarrassing ordeal.” Kunes also requested privacy for herself and her family and alleged that they have been harassed over the past several days and received death threats. The American Civil Liberties Union of Mississippi is also looking into complaints it has received about the incident, Candi Richardson, the organization’s director of communications and community engagement, said Monday.

articles.title: IBM’s biggest division ends most US foreign worker sponsorships
articles.summary: Announcement follows Trump administration crackdown on visa programmes for skilled foreign workers.
articles.body:
United States technology giant IBM has said it will stop sponsoring US foreign worker visas and green cards for most roles in its largest division.

A company spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday that its consultancy unit had opted to end sponsorship for most roles.

The company said its participation in US high-skilled visa programmes had been declining for years, adding that the decision came “as skill availability and client needs have evolved”.

IBM Consulting employs more than 150,000 of IBM’s 264,300-strong global workforce.

IBM has become less reliant on so-called H-1B visas for highly skilled foreign workers in recent years. Only 1,611 H-1B petitions were approved for the company in fiscal year 2026, according to data from US Citizenship and Immigration Services.

The announcement comes as the Trump administration has increased pressure on major companies to cut down on their highly skilled foreign workforce in the US. US President Donald Trump has claimed the programme is often subject to fraud and takes work away from skilled Americans and gives it to immigrants.

Last year, the administration announced it would require a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions.

The administration said in October it was suspending a number of tech companies from a programme that allows H-1B workers to apply for green cards, saying it was cracking down on fraud and ensuring American workers were not being laid off and replaced by foreigners.

The suspended companies included Adobe and top H-1B employers Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services and Microsoft.

The suspensions were announced within hours of Trump honouring Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

India-born Nadella was one of six business leaders honoured by Trump. Five were foreign-born US citizens, including Tesla boss Elon Musk, who was born in South Africa, and Google co-founder Sergey Brin, who immigrated from Russia with his family as a child.

articles.title: Look of the Week: Nvidia’s CEO appeared in a very stylish archival leather jacket. If only it were real
articles.summary: A now viral manipulated photo of the CEO sporting a luxe leather jacket speaks to the growing impossibility of distinguishing real from fake in the age of AI.
articles.body: When an image allegedly showing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in his first public appearance since reports of an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy punctured his public image and sent his company’s shares tumbling, it quickly went viral. Huang was sporting a different look than usual. Instead of his signature smooth motorcycle-style leather jacket, he wore a much more ostentatious, studded version that online commentators quickly identified as Hedi Slimane-era Saint Laurent, an-eye catching archival grail for a man under siege. There’s only one problem. “Those images are fake,” a spokesperson for Nvidia said in an email. The image’s proliferation speaks to the growing impossibility of distinguishing real from fake as AI tools — like the ones Nvidia’s chips power — further permeate our personal algorithms. In theory, it would have been a great (and distracting) look: a very flashy stepping out for a very difficult moment in the AI mogul’s career. “First person in history to have negative aura wearing archive Hedi,” read one comment with over a thousand likes on a post featuring the images, referring to Slimane, the French designer who served as Saint Laurent’s’s creative director from 2012 to 2016 before taking the reins at Celine until 2024. The images appear to be altered from a real image of Huang arriving at Seoul’s Gimpo International Airport in June. They were seemingly plausible in part because the jacket was a variation on Huang’s uniform. The AI leader is almost always seen in a slim-cut leather jacket. He has, he told CBS, close to 30 or 40 leather jackets. Like other tech leaders who have opted for uniforms in the mold of Steve Jobs’ Issey Miyake black turtlenecks, he cited the fact that wearing the same outfit makes it easier for him to focus his attention on bigger things (like building a technology quickly taking over huge swaths of the global economy). “Black is the absence of choice,” he told CBS. “That’s one decision made, one less thing to deal with. For everybody else, they probably have to make 3 or 4 decisions. I took that off my plate. It’s fantastic.” Huang’s classic leather jacket is an edgier, more striking look than the slouchy t-shirts favored by Mark Zuckerberg and Sam Altman. It’s the favored garment of bikers everywhere, James Dean wannabes, and anyone trying to embody an ideal of timeless cool. He occasionally wears variations, like a reptile-skin version he sported for a keynote speech at the 2026 Consumer Electronics Show. One of his pieces, a Tom Ford jacket touted as the “CEO’s Uniform” and the “Jensen Jacket,” was auctioned by Sotheby’s earlier this year, which described it as “a symbol of his leadership style embodying authenticity, ingenuity, persistence, courage and joy.” It sold for close to $1 million, roughly double the presale estimates. Huang, who has been married to his college sweetheart since 1985, has admitted to having an affair, saying he “hurt his wife and children,” but hasn’t named the other person involved. US intelligence have concluded in a classified memo issued in May that a close associate of Huang’s Alice Huang (no relation) was a Chinese intelligence asset. In interviews, he’s attributed his signature look to his wife Lori, who he told CBS buys his jackets for him. “I’m happy that my wife and daughter dress me,” he said in an interview for HP’s tech podcast “The Moment” in 2023.

articles.body: A 7-year-old girl with dual U.S. and Mexican citizenship was shot and killed during a Mexican security operation targeting an alleged cartel member, and her mother accused police officers aboard a helicopter of firing the deadly shot. Aranza Aidelany Pardo died Oct. 29 in Matamoros, a Mexican border city across from Brownsville, Texas. articles.title: US poll shows death penalty lost majority support for first time since 1971
articles.summary: Support for capital punishment has been declining in the US for years over concerns about fairness and racial bias.
articles.body:
A new Gallup poll has found that support for the death penalty in the United States has fallen below 50 percent, marking the first time that the controversial practice has lost majority support since 1971.

The poll released on Tuesday found that 49 percent of people said they are in favour of capital punishment for those convicted of murder, the lowest level since 1966, while 45 percent say they are opposed.

“While statistically similar to last year’s 52 percent, the latest update marks the first time support has been below the majority level since 1971, when it was also at 49 percent,” Gallup said in a statement.

Support for the death penalty has been declining for decades amid concerns about issues of fairness, racial bias, high costs, botched executions and the possibility of innocent people being put to death. Decades of scholarship have also cast doubt on the argument that capital punishment deters crime.

The latest Gallup poll found stark divides by age and partisan affiliation. While 54 percent of people aged 50 and older support the death penalty, that figure drops to just 39 percent for those younger the age of 30.

About 73 percent of Republicans are in favour, compared with 50 percent for independents and 28 percent for Democrats.

But all of those groups have seen support decline over the last three decades, dropping by 11 points for Republicans, 29 points for independents, and 47 points for Democrats since 1994, during the heyday of tough-on-crime politics in the US.

In that period, a punitive approach to criminal justice embraced by both parties transformed the US into one of the most prolific jailers on the planet and saw an increase in the number of crimes that qualified for execution.

A debate about the legacy of the policies championed during that era, including the death penalty, has been pushed forward by protests for racial justice in recent years.

While 27 US states still have the death penalty, 23 have done away with the practice and four have paused it through executive action, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit research group.

Many states that still have capital punishment on the books have gone years without carrying out an execution, and lengthy appeals processes have meant that many prisoners spend years or even decades on death row.

President Donald Trump has been an exception to the move away from capital punishment, overseeing a massive increase in federal executions during his first term in office and promising to continue using it during his second.

The prevalence of botched executions, such as that of Christa Pike via failed lethal injection in the state of Tennessee last month, has also raised questions about whether the practice violates the constitutional prohibition on cruel and unusual punishment.

articles.title: UNIFIL patrol comes under fire in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: UNIFIL said on Tuesday that ‘about a dozen rounds’ were fired at one of its patrols, without identifying the assailants.
articles.body:
A United Nations peacekeeping force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) patrol has come under fire in southern Lebanon, the force said.

UNIFIL said on Tuesday that “about a dozen rounds” were fired at one of its patrols near Wadi Jilu, in Lebanon’s Tyre district, without specifying the entity behind the shooting.

The patrol returned fire, after which the shooting stopped. UNIFIL reported no casualties and called for an investigation.

“We reiterate the obligation under international law for all actors to ensure the safety and security of UN personnel and property at all times. Deliberate attacks on peacekeepers are violations of Security Council resolution 1701 and international humanitarian law,” UNIFIL said.

UNIFIL is a peacekeeping mission established by the UN Security Council in March 1978, days after Israel invaded Lebanon.

The force has acted as a buffer between Israel and Lebanon ever since, but its presence has been unable to prevent several rounds of conflict, including the latest between Israel and Hezbollah.

Israel continues to occupy swaths of southern Lebanon, despite a so-called ceasefire and a US-brokered framework agreement through which the Israeli military would withdraw from those areas and the Lebanese army would move in to disarm Hezbollah.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said on Tuesday that the G7 foreign ministers agreed on “the need to avoid a security void” in Lebanon after the UNIFIL mandate expires at the end of 2026.

The foreign ministers backed “the need to move quickly toward a new security architecture”, Barrot said after the group met in Paris.

However, the French foreign minister acknowledged that there had been no breakthrough regarding replacing UNIFIL, which comprises some 7,500 personnel from nearly 50 countries.

The UN Security Council last year voted, under US pressure, to end UNIFIL’s mandate on December 31, 2026. Lebanese officials have called for the mandate to be extended.

articles.title: How Paraguay’s banking crisis toppled a staunch Trump ally in Latin America
articles.summary: Paraguay’s ousted President Santiago Peña is facing up to 15 years in prison after the collapse of a major bank triggered the country’s biggest political crisis in years.
articles.body: Paraguay’s ousted President Santiago Peña is facing up to 15 years in prison after the collapse of a major bank triggered the country’s biggest political crisis in years. Digital lender Ueno Bank shut down last week due to solvency concerns, leaving millions of customers unable to access their money. Peña, who until last year had business ties to the bank, submitted his resignation after its collapse, but Congress voted to impeach the president instead. The ousted leader, an economist and supporter of US President Donald Trump, is now facing criminal charges over the crisis, with prosecutors alleging a conflict of interest. He’s being held in pretrial detention at a military facility as prosecutors continue to investigate him. The crisis has shocked the country, with many people wondering how things could have spiraled out of control so quickly and how the turmoil will be resolved. Here’s what we know so far. How the scandal unfolded Paraguay’s central bank voted last Monday to put Ueno Bank into resolution after finding that its solvency ratio had fallen below the required minimum. The following day, the central bank seized the lender, freezing the accounts of nearly 2.9 million customers in a country of 6.1 million people. After days of protests, anxiety and long lines at the bank, Peña announced that he would resign on Thursday, saying he wanted to give Paraguayans peace of mind and restore stability. Both chambers of Congress convened a joint session to consider his resignation, but it was adjourned without a decision after several lawmakers walked out in the middle of the vote. If lawmakers had accepted his resignation, he would have been given immunity and special protections. Instead, the lower chamber voted unanimously to impeach him on Thursday afternoon, saying he should face charges over the financial crisis. The Senate followed up by voting to remove him from office on Friday. Vice President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as president soon after the vote. What charges does Peña face? Peña has been charged with breach of trust and administration for personal gain, with each charge carrying up to 10 years in prison, according to prosecutor Nancy Salomón. If he’s found guilty of both charges, the second conviction is halved, meaning he could potentially serve up to 15 years, according to Paraguay’s penal code. The former president, who denies any wrongdoing, held shares in Grupo Vázquez, Ueno Bank’s main shareholder, and sold his stake last year. Prosecutors allege that during his presidency, Peña “intervened in decisions related to the placement, renewal and maintenance of public and pension funds in Ueno Bank, an entity with whose business group he allegedly maintained economic and corporate ties.” Peña was initially placed under house arrest but was later transferred to a military facility for pretrial detention. CNN has contacted the former president and his lawyer Ricardo Preda for comment on the charges. Prosecutors also say the bank allegedly granted Peña “two simultaneous loans” in May 2024 for $580,000 “to finance the construction” of his luxurious summer home in San Bernardino, about 50 kilometers (31 miles) from the capital Asunción. On Sunday, authorities carried out a search warrant at the property, where they discovered a “highly sophisticated security vault.” Salomón told CNN they were expected to open it on Tuesday. Authorities also discovered computers, devices and potentially important documents at Peña’s residence. US ties to Paraguay Peña was one of US President Donald Trump’s staunchest allies in Latin America. A member of the conservative Colorado Party, he aligned with many of Trump’s political priorities, particularly immigration and security. Earlier this year, the White House invited him to attend a summit in Miami along with other right-wing Latin American leaders who are close to Trump. The White House said the gathering was meant to “promote freedom, security and prosperity.” Peña had forged strong ties with the Trump administration through deals on defense and regional coordination, such as the “safe third country” agreement, which allows asylum seekers from the US to be transferred to Paraguay. In response to Peña’s announced resignation on Thursday, a US State Department spokesperson said the relationship between both countries remains strong: “We remain committed to the enduring relationship between the American and Paraguayan people and look forward to continuing our close cooperation on shared priorities.” What we know about the new president Peña was succeeded by his vice president, Pedro Alliana, who survived an impeachment vote in the lower chamber of Congress on Thursday. Alliana had previously served as a congressman, leader of the Chamber of Deputies and governor of Ñeembucú. Before joining the Colorado Party, he was a businessman and an athlete who formed part of the Paraguayan national basketball team. He will now be the country’s president for the next two years. Upon being sworn in on Friday, Alliana vowed to assume the position with “humility, responsibility and a deep commitment to all Paraguayans.” On Tuesday, Alliana held a roundtable meeting with his ministers to discuss a path forward. “I ordered the ministers of the Executive Branch to work as a team, with austerity and zero tolerance for corruption. The state’s resources belong to the people and must be managed responsibly,” he said on X. What happens next? Paraguayans have welcomed Peña’s impeachment, but many are upset that he was succeeded by his own vice president. In parts of the capital, demonstrators have demanded the ouster of every member of government, using the rallying cry “Out with them all!” Alliana has overhauled several government ministries by appointing new leaders. Among them is Jorge Schreiner, who was approved by Congress as the new president of the central bank, replacing Carlos Carvallo whom prosecutors have also charged in the Ueno case. Prosecutors say the goal is for Ueno Bank depositors to recover all their savings. However, many questions remain about the future of the country. Analysts say Paraguay’s reputation as a stable South American economy has taken a hit and the banking crisis could impact other parts of society, including the labor market and the social security system. Schreiner told CNN that he is committed to restoring Paraguay’s credibility, which he acknowledged is “quite damaged.” “It’s possible to recover. It will take us a while, but we restore that,” he said. Alliana said that recovering lost funds will be a priority. Earlier, he announced that the government had paid most of Ueno’s customers roughly $330 million from Paraguay’s Deposit Guarantee Fund, a safety net established to protect depositors in the event of insolvency. “We will work until every family regains the peace of mind they deserve,” he said.

articles.title: Whoopi Goldberg lectures Democrats over infighting about leadership, warns 'get your stuff together'
articles.summary: Whoopi Goldberg called out Democratic infighting over congressional leadership demanding the party focus on gas prices and SNAP benefits.
articles.body: "The View" co-host Whoopi Goldberg admonished congressional Democrats on Tuesday over their public debate about whether to support Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., as party leaders. "This is my two cents," Goldberg said, after the show played several clips of Democrats discussing their leadership opinions. "I don’t want to hear this from you right now. I want to know what all of you are, all of you Democrats, what are your plans for the first 100 days? I don’t care if you’ve been there forever or just got there. What are your plans?" Goldberg suggested several priorities for Democrats, including lowering gas and grocery prices, restoring funding for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits and reuniting separated families. "We put you in there to clean house, to make sure that the government works the way the people want it to work," Goldberg said. "I don’t want to hear all this infighting because then you become the distraction, and then you become no better than the Republicans were. So just get your stuff together. All of you." HOUSE PASSES SENATE DHS FUNDING BILL AFTER JOHNSON REVERSES COURSE ON 76-DAY SHUTDOWN STANDOFF Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin predicted Jeffries would become the next House speaker and said only the "far left" was questioning his leadership. She also argued that Schumer "should go the way of Nancy Pelosi." Griffin argued Schumer should declare victory after helping recruit and elect several Democratic candidates, then step aside for a new generation of leaders. Sunny Hostin, who previously criticized Schumer and called for his removal in November 2025, suggested he should remain in leadership and become Senate Majority Leader. "I mean, Chuck Schumer led and made sure there wasn’t a government shutdown. He did whip up, he kept the Democratic caucus together," Hostin said during the show on Tuesday. "He got all of these wonderful candidates. Why not let him lead the party because he knows how to do it? My fear is you get someone in that’s new, that doesn’t really know what they’re doing, doesn’t know how to deal with Trump, doesn’t know how to build a consensus." Several incoming Democratic senators have said they will not support Schumer for party leader, including Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton and Sen.-elect Troy Jackson. WATCH: JEFFRIES FACES UNCERTAINTY FROM INCOMING DEMOCRATS AS HOUSE SPEAKER VOTE APPROACHES Other Democrats, including Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have called for a "conversation" about the party's leadership. Schumer's and Jeffries' offices did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Whoopi is right about the scale of this. Democrats just got handed a mandate to make people’s lives better, not to turn the first month into an internal dispute about Chuck Schumer. If members think he should go, say why, vote, and move on." However, Schroff said, "At the same time, ‘stop the infighting’ cannot become code for ‘nobody challenges the old guard.’" "Of course Schumer deserves credit for some of these wins and the overall strategy," he continued. "Let’s be honest, even many Dem insiders didn’t think the blue wave would be this big and Schumer and Jeffries absolutely deserve credit. At the same time, Democrats just elected a younger, more restless coalition, so the old leadership should expect to be questioned. That’s normal." Goldberg issued a warning to Democrats last week after the party swept in the midterm elections and will take back control of the House and the Senate in January. articles.title: 'Unable to manage fridges': Iran mocks France after Paris blames Tehran for supermarket cyberattack
articles.summary: A diplomatic row has erupted between France and Iran after Paris accused an Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) cyber unit of carrying out attacks
articles.body: A diplomatic row has erupted between France and Iran after Paris accused an Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) cyber unit of carrying out attacks that disrupted refrigeration systems across hundreds of supermarkets in France. Tehran has rejected the allegations, with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi mocking the French government for being "unable to manage fridges".French authorities said a joint investigation by intelligence and cybersecurity agencies had identified Shahid Kaveh, an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the IRGC's Electronic Warfare and Cyber Defence Organization, as responsible for the attacks. The operation targeted temperature controls in commercial refrigeration systems on the night of October 11-12, affecting around 700 establishments across France.According to French authorities, the hackers remotely altered the temperature settings of refrigeration units, resulting in widespread food spoilage worth tens of millions of euros. At least 15 fires were also reported after refrigeration units were affected. Besides supermarkets, the attacks targeted small butcher shops, a slaughterhouse and food-processing factories.In a statement, the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs described the operation as an act of "unprecedented scale and aggressiveness" and said it was the first offensive cyber campaign aimed purely at causing physical damage on French soil."Following investigations, France is now in a position to attribute these destructive actions to Iran: they were carried out by SHAHID KAVEH, an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Electronic Warfare and Cyber Defence Organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps," the ministry said.The French ministry also described the group as a "persistent threat to our critical infrastructure", arguing that the operation violated international law and United Nations norms governing responsible state conduct in cyberspace.The investigation also named three alleged associates of the cyber unit: Hamid Reza Lashgarian, Mahdi Lashgarian and Reza Salarvand, according to a report by Reuters.Responding to the allegations, Araghchi accused the French government of shifting blame to external actors to deflect attention from domestic grievances. He also criticised Paris over its position on the conflict in Gaza."Unable to manage fridges let alone addressing grievances of its people, French government is shifting blame for its failures onto others," Araghchi said in a post on social media platform X."Yes, Iran is powerful. But unlike France, we do not exercise power via support for massacres in Gaza or bombings of schools and hospitals," he added.France also recalled previous cyber operations it attributed to Iran, including attacks targeting the satirical magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and attempted disruptions surrounding the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games.French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador had been summoned to the Foreign Ministry to receive a formal protest. articles.title: US House Republicans block Pete Hegseth impeachment effort
articles.summary: Hegseth has been accused of spearheading war on Iran without required congressional approval.
articles.body:
Republicans in the United States House of Representatives have nixed an effort to advance the impeachment of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, following a midterm election in which voters vented frustrations over the Iran war Hegseth has helped spearhead.

The lower house of the US Congress voted in favour of a motion to refer the impeachment charges to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee in a procedural vote on Tuesday, effectively killing an effort to remove Hegseth from his position led by Republican Representative Thomas Massie.

That push also won support from Democratic representatives, setting up a test of whether Republican lawmakers would break with the Trump administration and distance themselves from the unpopular war after a rebuke at the polls.

The final vote on Tuesday was 211 in favour and 204 against, with Massie the lone Republican to vote against it. The result means that Republicans will be able to slow-walk the process and can avoid a direct vote on the eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth, which cover issues such as the Iran war.

“The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED!” Trump said in a social media post following the vote. “Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favour of Pete.”

Regardless of the outcome of Tuesday’s vote, an impeachment conviction in the US Senate, where it would require a two-thirds vote and Republicans have a 53-seat majority, was seen as unlikely.

Massie’s resolution included eight separate articles of impeachment , accusing the combative Pentagon chief of launching an illegal war against Iran without congressional approval and overseeing a campaign of strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking vessels that legal scholars say are extrajudicial killings .

Hegseth has denounced the resolution as “sabotage” and a “farce”, while US President Donald Trump and prominent members of his administration expressed their continued support for him.

Speculation about Hegseth’s position within the administration has circulated as polls suggest that voters partly blame the war for surging prices of goods such as gasoline and groceries, and has grown stronger after Republicans faced punishing losses in the midterm elections.

“Is he being truthful in the way the war is going?” outgoing Republican Senator Joni Ernst said of Hegseth on Tuesday.

articles.title: Why David Walliams' unprecedented legal battle to stay anonymous failed
articles.summary: The 55-year-old was named in reports by ITV News and the Guardian on Tuesday after losing a court bid to stop allegations being made public.
articles.body:
David Walliams' unprecedented legal battle not to be named in relation to allegations against him went downhill as he tried to secure a permanent injunction.

He was named by the Guardian and ITN because he had no sound legal reason to prevent the news organisations' investigation from being published. In response to the allegations included, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

The 55-year-old's bid for an injunction had been an open secret from the start after what would have normally been an anonymised application briefly appeared under his own name on a court cases register.

His exceptionally unusual attempt to gag the media - forever - became clear at the full trial last month - but that's when his bid to remain anonymous got worse.

In court, his lawyers did not claim that the investigation would be disclosing legally confidential or private information the journalists were not entitled to - two avenues often trod to silence reporters.

Instead lawyers for Walliams argued that such was the threat to his life from publication that the court itself would be breaching his human rights, were it to allow the story to go ahead.

This was, the court ultimately concluded, unheard of.

Under Article 2 of the European Convention on Human Rights, the British state has a duty to take reasonable steps to try to protect life where they can do so and, importantly, where a particular body has an actual responsibility to do so.

There's no expectation that a state agency can save all lives in all circumstances - but it must show it has done its best if it is clear it had a responsibility to act.

The most obvious example of this law in practice is that the police must try to act on credible intelligence of a threat to life, even if the intended victim is a gangster.

But that duty, and how it should be applied in the real world, is also why Walliams lost: he was expecting the wrong public body to be doing the protecting.

The High Court's Mr Justice Nicklin said that the responsibility to try to protect the comedian and author's life was on clinicians and the hospital he had already been taken to. He had been detained for his own protection, meaning the state was already trying to meet its obligation to protect him from harm.

The court could not do that protecting because it had not taken responsibility for Walliams' psychiatric treatment or safety. Its role was to decide the legal dispute between Walliams and the news organisations.

Walliams' lawyers had suggested that there might be a right to private family life issue in the case but the judge said there had been no evidence to detail that, and he had to take into account the media's right to freedom of speech to publish what was described in court as a detailed investigation in the public interest.

If the media were wrong about their claims, Walliams could later sue for defamation - the way that any wrong party seeks redress against journalists.

David Walliams accused of sexual misconduct after losing injunction bid

Watch: What we know about the allegations against David Walliams

David Walliams' career and controversies including Britain's Got Talent and Little Britain

After Walliams lost last week, and the court's judgment underlines how seriously it considered the risks to him to be, Mr Justice Nicklin asked whether there were plans for an appeal.

But Walliams had not been able to give his lawyers instructions on how to proceed.

"There is a degree of urgency - the court has moved exceptionally quickly to accommodate this trial and produce this judgment," said Mr Justice Nicklin. "It is slightly concerning that there is not an ability to proceed today. I don't understand really. If I was satisfied that there were compelling reasons why permission to appeal should be granted I could say so now. "

Sara Mansoori KC, Walliams' counsel, said the case raised "novel issues of law based on unusual facts" but because of the vulnerable nature of her client - in hospital - she needed more time.

The judge gave Walliams until 16:30 GMT on Monday to come up with some proper grounds to challenge his decision. Those papers were never filed.

The failure to launch an appeal bid meant that ITN and the Guardian were free to publish.

While all this had been going on in court - there was a social media-sized elephant in the room. No end of people were posting 'It's David Walliams' and wondering why we bona fide journalists were not saying the same.

When the courts in the UK order that someone should remain anonymous, that order applies to all forms of publishing and broadcasting. It matters not whether the publication is in a newspaper or online - it is still publication. That is why bona fide journalists who understand the law did not wade in.

But there is a massive practical issue: how far does the writ of English law run in cyber space?

One judge I recently addressed over a reporting restriction issue described social media as a "wild west". That comment underlines the concern among legal professionals.

But the question is how to enforce injunctions in an age of rapid fire digital gossip?

If a newsroom were to breach an order, the nature of a large media organisation's audience means that publication would be seen by judges to be rather grave and the editor would likely be up in court.

One random user of X publishing the suspected identity of an anonymised person by passing on gossip is obviously less impactful. If Chad from Utah reposts Dorothy from Liverpool's gossip, the chances of being hauled before a judge are even more remote.

But what happens when thousands of people are all saying the same - and then their claims, perhaps based on a kernel of unreportable truth, are magnified by AI summaries and algorithms dripping content into phones?

At that point, mathematically speaking the impact is greater than one single newsroom breaching an injunction.

The public's perception of the Walliams case was complicated because his name became known from the start - but the furious gossip over who "PPT" really was shows there is an existential threat to how courts try to control information to prevent harm. And it's not clear whether they have any answer to it.

articles.title: Russia expels Moldovan diplomat in tit-for-tat move
articles.summary: Relations between Moscow and Chisinau have worsened since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
articles.body:
Russia has expelled a Moldovan diplomat in retaliation for Chisinau’s expulsion of a Russian embassy employee over the crash of a drone in Moldova.

Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesday that it had summoned Moldova’s ambassador, Lilian Darii, and informed him that a member of the Moldovan embassy’s staff had been declared unacceptable “on the basis of the principle of reciprocity”.

“A strong protest was lodged with the ambassador after the Moldovan authorities on October 23 declared an employee of the Russian embassy in Chisinau persona non grata,” the ministry said in a statement.

It said Moldova’s decision was made “under the formal pretext of the alleged discovery on the territory of the republic of debris of an unmanned aerial vehicle carrying explosives”, calling it “another unfriendly step”.

The ministry said the “true goal” of the move was “to further undermine the centuries-long history of Russian-Moldovan relations”.

Last month, Moldovan President Maia Sandu said a “Russian attack drone” had violated the country’s airspace and “crashed near homes and an energy facility”.

Moldova then declared a staff member of the Russian embassy “persona non grata”.

Drones have penetrated Moldovan territory on multiple occasions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Since then, Russia’s relations with former Soviet states, such as Moldova, have hit an all-time low, compounded by the push by some of those states to join the European Union.

On Sunday, Moldova officially launched a new power line connecting the country to neighbouring Romania and the European grid to reduce its dependence on Russian energy.

The 400-kilovolt extra-high-voltage line, which runs from the city of Vulcanesti to Chisinau, allows Moldova to cut reliance on the Cuciurgan thermal power plant in Transnistria.

Other European-aligned states in the Black Sea region say they are experiencing renewed attacks allegedly carried out by Moscow, such as a drone strike that sank a cargo ship off Romania’s Black Sea coast in October.
